verdict.rationale: Twenty documents the pieces an agent would use: an MCP server, REST/GraphQL APIs that support record updates, email and calendar sync linked to CRM records, and in-CRM AI agents that run multi-step tasks under role permissions. However, no documented flow shows an agent reading email or meeting signals and updating deal stages or next steps. The closest evidence is a mention of scoring opportunities from engagement patterns. Missing for 10: a documented agent workflow that updates opportunity stage or next steps from email/meeting signals, evidence that email and calendar data is exposed through the API or MCP, details of the MCP server's tools, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent update deal stages and next steps from email and meeting signals via the API or MCP server

citations.quote: Both REST and GraphQL support batching up to 60 records per request — create, update, or delete.
Emails and calendar events automatically appear on the relevant CRM records.
AI agents that work autonomously within your CRM — answering questions, enriching records, and executing multi-step tasks within your permission model.
Score opportunities based on engagement patterns
